title: Sourcing terms, billing pathfinding & onboarding clarity workshop
summary: Workshop to align on MSA/DPA exceptions, preferred billing path (Redwood hosted vs VPC egress), privileged keying options, and an initial pilot scope with acceptance criteria. Legal asked for audit log retention and KMS details; procurement wants cost predictability and data residency assurances.
topics: KMS / privileged keying and escrow discussion
transcript:
Header: 2026-01-06 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee - Redwood AE; Anika Patel - Redwood SE; Samir Rao - Redwood Solutions; Jared Kim - Thermalix Procurement; Priya Menon - Thermalix Legal; Rafael Ortiz - CTO; Ellen Sato - FinOps

Summary: quick workshop, fairly packed; lots of redlines and a few pricing asks that need follow-up. Note — some ASR glitches in places (Redwood Dedicated heard as 'Redwood Dedicato').

[00:00] Marcus: Hey everybody, thanks for joining—happy new year—I'll kick us off. Agenda is MSA/DPA redline walk, billing routing (hosted vs vpc egress), and pilot acceptance.
[00:18] Jared: thanks Marcus. For procurement side we just need clarity on committed usage tiers and where egress fees land. Also timeline for security docs.
[00:34] Priya: yes and from legal, the DPA we sent has a couple of nonstandard clauses we want to check — data deletion, subprocessor list and a 30 day notification for changes.
[00:50] Anika: got it, we can go through each one. Important to call out: for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and on-prem options, but the path and billing differ.
[01:10] Rafael: quick question — we have a compliance requirement to keep logs for 7 years, is that feasible?
[01:22] Samir: long retention like 7 years is unusual but technically possible; we need to look at retention tiering and cost. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 and retained as you need, that separates the storage cost.
[01:40] Ellen: ok so storage cost is separate — procurement wants ballpark numbers for 100K inference requests/mo.
[01:55] Marcus: we'll follow up with an example cost sheet. For the call now, let's walk the DPA redline Priya sent.
[02:08] Priya: thanks. Clause 4.2 — data residency. We need explicit EU-only processing for EU customer data and contractual guarantee. Right now the DPA references region routing but not a contractual commitment.
[02:30] Anika: we have region pinning for models and routing policies, we can commit to EU-only processing for EU-identified traffic in Dedicated or Private. On hosted, we can route to EU region but there are edge cases.
[02:50] Priya: so hosted still leaves a slight exposure. Legal would prefer Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads.
[03:05] Marcus: yes that's typical. We should map that to the MSA — hosted service terms under Section 2, Dedicated/Private under Section 3 with an SLA addendum.
[03:20] Jared: about SLA — what are your uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated? We need numbers for procurement review.
[03:32] Anika: Dedicated has a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency targets per model tier—e.g., 95th p95 token latency under X ms on A100 equivalent pools. We'll send the performance profile matrix.
[03:50] Rafael: what about fallbacks — if Dedicated is saturated do requests go to hosted and does that change billing or data residency?
[04:05] Samir: we have smart routing options. Default can be no-fallback for Dedicated (fail closed), or you can enable fallback to hosted which would change the data residency guarantee and billing.
[04:22] Priya: that behavior must be explicit in the contract and no automatic failover without prior written approval.
[04:32] Marcus: noted — we'll mark that as an MSA item.
[04:41] Jared: billing path — procurement's main worry is surprise egress fees when we use a VPC connection. Can you explain the common patterns?
[04:55] Anika: two common patterns: 1) Hosted API: all compute and storage in Redwood cloud, billed per token/embedding unit; egress minimal. 2) VPC/Private: customer runs private route with dedicated capacity and egress (network) billed separately; if you bring your own cloud storage or KMS there may be cross-account egress costs.
[05:18] Ellen: so for example if models are loaded in our VPC and we fetch from S3, that S3 egress is our cloud provider's charge, not Redwood's?
[05:28] Samir: correct. We can offer a blended price to include expected egress if you want a single invoice; that is typically a committed contract line item.
[05:40] Jared: blended price sounds good but procurement will need the assumptions and a cap.
[05:48] Marcus: we'll propose a pilot rate with a clearly stated cap and overage rate.
[05:54] Priya: on KMS — clause about privileged keying: we want HSM-backed customer keys and controls for key rotation. Are you supporting customer-owned keys?
[06:10] Anika: yes, in Private you can use your KMS/HSM through our key proxy. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via our KMS integration but truly private HSM in-hosted mode requires Dedicated with private key wrapping.
[06:30] Rafael: any escrow implications? Our security team asked about key escrow in the event of emergency access.
[06:39] Samir: we generally avoid escrow; for enterprise engagements we can define an emergency key recovery process with strict controls and audit logs. That will be in the privileged key appendix.
[06:56] Priya: please give sample language — we need to review for compliance.
[07:02] Marcus: we'll share a privileged-keys appendix draft and a sample key recovery workflow.
[07:12] Ellen: procurement — can we get a 60 day onboarding runway and a pilot that lasts 30 days after onboarding? We need to coordinate finance and security reviews.
[07:23] Marcus: yes typical timeline — 60 days for provisioning and security checks, 30-day pilot.
[07:30] Jared: pilot acceptance criteria? We need measurable SLAs and a quality bar.
[07:36] Anika: pilot success criteria propose: 1) latency under p95 target for key routes, 2) 99% successful calls with no data leakage incidents, 3) integration of SSO and test KMS rotations, 4) cost within agreed pilot budget.
[07:56] Priya: legal also needs a remediation path and a termination right if PII exposure occurs.
[08:05] Samir: we can draft a pilot addendum with those items.
[08:12] [08:12] Jared: procurement question — are there minimum commitments for Dedicated?
[08:18] Marcus: Dedicated typically has a monthly commit (e.g., GPU-hour commit) with a 12 month baseline in enterprise deals, but we can do a short-term pilot with monthly true-ups.
[08:30] Rafael: how does model version pinning work? We want to pin a specific quantized model for production.
[08:39] Anika: you can pin a model version at route level. Rollouts can be canary or A/B. If you pin we guarantee that version stays unless you request a change or we have security critical fixes.
[08:55] Priya: our legal redline asked for a security bulletin window — 30 days notice before non-critical changes, immediate for critical fixes with explanation.
[09:08] Marcus: reasonable. We'll include a change notification timeline in the SLA appendix.
[09:16] Ellen: billing detail again — can you provide sample invoices showing blended vs separate egress?
[09:24] Samir: yes we'll attach sample invoices and a model that maps calls to cost line items.
[09:31] Priya: DPA clause about subprocessors: we want a 30 day right to object to new subprocessors and an obligation to notify.
[09:44] Anika: we notify for new subprocessors; the right to object is reasonable but we usually handle objections via mitigation or replacement commitments.
[09:55] Rafael: also performance benchmarks — can we run a short benchmark in our environment? We want to test model latency on our typical documents.
[10:05] Marcus: yes we can run a lab benchmark — SE will run a workload replay using your prompt set. We'll need a small dataset and a timeslot.
[10:16] Priya: legal question: will the benchmark data get retained by Redwood? We need assurances it will be deleted after the benchmark.
[10:27] Anika: benchmarks run in a temporary environment, logs exported to your S3 and we purge local copies; we'll include deletion commitments in the benchmark statement.
[10:40] Jared: procurement — pricing approvals: we will need full TCO for three scenarios: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (on-prem).
[10:49] Marcus: understood. We'll provide TCO sheets and a recommended path.
[10:54] Ellen: can you also give a sensitivity analysis if token usage doubles?
[11:00] Samir: yes, we'll include spike scenarios.
[11:06] [11:06] Marcus: switching tracks — audit and compliance: do you need SOC2 or ISO attestation evidence?
[11:12] Priya: yes SOC2 Type II is required. Also we may request penetration test reports.
[11:20] Samir: we can provide SOC2 report under NDA and discuss scope of pentest — enterprise customers sometimes do a joint pentest.
[11:30] Rafael: how are incident notifications handled? RTO/RPO?
[11:35] Anika: in SLA we define incident severity, RTO for critical incidents, and notification timelines (T+1 hour for Sev1). We'll share the incident runbook.
[11:48] Priya: redline: liability cap — we want a higher cap for data breaches. Standard MSA proposes a multiple of fees; we want carveouts for willful misconduct.
[12:02] Marcus: we'll pull the legal team on suggested language — can you send exact preferred phrasing, Priya?
[12:09] Priya: will do. We'll attach an alternative clause in the doc comment.
[12:15] Rafael: any references or customer case studies for similar regulated customers?
[12:22] Marcus: yes we have a healthcare customer (anonymized) and a fintech with private deployment; we'll share a redacted case study and reference contacts.
[12:35] Jared: procurement timeline: we target contract signed in 90 days, pilot in month 4. Is that feasible?
[12:43] Samir: feasible if legal review is 2-3 weeks and procurement approvals 4-6 weeks, we can hit that timeline.
[12:53] Ellen: ok good. Now quick run through of immediate asks and owners.
[13:00] Marcus: action items: we'll list and then wrap.
[13:05] [13:05] Marcus: action item 1: Redwood to provide sample invoice and blended pricing model. Owner: Marcus. Due: 2026-01-13.
[13:20] Anika: action item 2: SE to run benchmark plan and provide data deletion/retention language. Owner: Anika. Due: 2026-01-20.
[13:35] Samir: action item 3: Solutions to draft privileged-key appendix and emergency key recovery workflow. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-01-15.
[13:48] Priya: action item 4: Customer to send exact MSA/DPA preferred language for liability and subprocessors. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-01-11.
[13:59] Jared: action item 5: Procurement to review pilot budget and send approval. Owner: Jared. Due: 2026-01-14.
[14:12] Marcus: next steps — we'll send a meeting packet with the items above and proposed redline responses.
[14:20] Rafael: one more item: is there an ops contact for day-to-day?
[14:25] Marcus: CSM will be assigned once contract is signed; we'll introduce them in the onboarding packet.
[14:33] Ellen: thanks all — that helps.
[14:36] [14:36] Marcus: quick recap verbally: Redwood to share blended pricing and invoice samples, privileged-key appendix, SE benchmark plan & deletion language, and performance matrix. Customer to share legal preferred clauses and pilot budget. We'll reconvene after the docs are shared.
[14:55] Priya: noted.
[15:00] Marcus: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Note: ASR glitches noted where product names looked odd — e.g., 'Redwood Dedicato' in minutes 02:xx appears as recognition artifact.
